item.title: New AWS automation simplifies activation of Bedrock private‑pricing entitlements across organizations
item.description:
New AWS automation simplifies activation of Bedrock private‑pricing entitlements across organizations

Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements simplifies multi‑account access to third‑party AI models by allowing a single subscription from a central account and distribution across an organization. After a private pricing offer is accepted, AWS Marketplace creates a license in AWS License Manager, which must be activated. AWS now offers two ways to activate these entitlements.

🔍 Overview

  • Managed entitlements let you subscribe once from a central account and distribute access to third‑party models across your organization.
  • Private Pricing Offers let you negotiate custom rates for third‑party models on Amazon Bedrock.
  • Once an eligible private offer is accepted, AWS Marketplace creates a license in AWS License Manager that starts in a Disabled state.

🛠️ Activation Options

Path When to use Core behavior
Lightweight script One‑time, no‑infrastructure fix for trusted licenses Lists received licenses and prints a dry‑run plan
CDK automation Ongoing, event‑driven processing Verifies sellers, creates distributed grants, retries activation as needed

⚙️ How the CDK Automation Works

  • Amazon EventBridge rule listens for AWS Marketplace agreement events on the default event bus in us-east-1. It matches source aws.agreement-marketplace and detail type Purchase Agreement Created - Acceptor, then invokes the Lambda function.
  • AWS Lambda function receives the agreement event, checks the seller against an allow‑list, discovers the associated license, creates the distributed grant, and requests activation with CreateGrantVersion(Status=ACTIVE).
  • The CDK stack is deployed in the AWS Organizations management account using Python 3.12+, the AWS CLI, and AWS CDK v2.
  • The stack retries activation when License Manager reports that more time is required.

📋 Key Details

  • Grants can target the whole organization, selected organizational units (OUs), or specific accounts.
  • In AWS Organizations with all features enabled, organization‑level grants are auto‑accepted but remain Disabled until you activate them.
  • Negotiated pricing applies only after the grant reaches ACTIVE or WORKFLOW_COMPLETED.
  • SaaS products are out of scope for this automation.
  • Confirm that the private offer is for a License Manager‑backed Bedrock model before running the automation.

🚀 Availability

  • Requires an AWS Organizations management account in us-east-1.
  • All Organization features must be enabled.
  • Requires Python 3.12+, AWS CLI, and AWS CDK v2 configured.
  • Works with third‑party AI models on Amazon Bedrock that are offered through AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers.

#AWS #AmazonBedrock #LicenseManager #CDK

Source: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AWS Cloud Development Kit Enables Infrastructure Definition Using Modern Programming Languages
item.description:
AWS Cloud Development Kit Enables Infrastructure Definition Using Modern Programming Languages

The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) is an open-source software development framework designed to define cloud infrastructure in code and provision it through AWS CloudFormation. It offers high-level object-oriented abstractions to define AWS resources imperatively using several modern programming languages.

🔍 Overview

The CDK allows developers to encapsulate AWS best practices within infrastructure definitions using a library of infrastructure constructs. This approach aims to reduce the complexity and glue-logic typically required when integrating various AWS services. By using the framework, developers can share infrastructure definitions without managing boilerplate logic.

🧩 How it works

Developers use the CDK framework in one of the supported programming languages to build components through a specific hierarchy:

  • Constructs: Reusable cloud components that encapsulate the details of how to use AWS.
  • Stacks: Compositions of constructs grouped together.
  • CDK App: The final application formed by one or more stacks.

Developers interact with their applications using the AWS CDK CLI. The CLI allows for the synthesis of artifacts such as AWS CloudFormation Templates, the deployment of stacks to development AWS accounts, and the ability to “diff” against a deployed stack to understand the impact of code changes.

⚙️ Key details

The AWS Construct Library includes modules for each AWS service. These modules are assigned stability designations that determine how they are updated:

Stability Designation Versioning Policy
Experimental Modules currently being built; may have breaking API changes in any release.
Stable Adheres to semantic versioning; breaking changes can only occur in major releases.

🚀 Availability

The AWS CDK is available for several programming languages with specific environment requirements:

Language Requirements
JavaScript / TypeScript Node.js >= 20.x
Python Python >= 3.8
Java Java >= 8 and Maven >= 3.5.4
.NET .NET >= 8.0
Go Go >= 1.16.4

Third-party language versions are supported until their vendor or community End Of Life (EOL). The AWS CDK CLI can be installed or updated via npm and requires Node.js >= 14.15.0, though using a version in Active LTS is recommended.

#AWS #CDK #InfrastructureAsCode #DevOps #CloudComputing

Source: aws/aws-cdk
